content.intro: In this lesson, you will study java language features by version with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you evaluate upgrades using compatibility evidence instead of assuming every release feature is stable. In this lesson, focus on java 8: lambdas, streams, and modern date/time apis and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A lambda provides an implementation of a functional interface. Prefer a named helper when it improves readability, and avoid unexpected shared-state mutation in callbacks. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect java 8: lambdas, streams, and modern date/time apis with java 9: modules before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Java 8: lambdas, streams, and modern date/time APIs
items.text: A lambda provides an implementation of a functional interface. Prefer a named helper when it improves readability, and avoid unexpected shared-state mutation in callbacks.

items.title: Java 9: modules
items.text: Packages organize names and access boundaries; the module system adds explicit module dependencies and exports. Keep public API surface intentional and verify classpath/module-path settings when troubleshooting.

items.title: Java 10: local variable type inference
items.text: A variable has a declared type and a scope. Initialize local variables before reading them; fields have defined default values, but relying on defaults can hide missing business logic.

items.title: Java 14: switch expressions
items.text: Control flow decides which statements run and how often. Make conditions precise, set clear loop termination conditions, and test zero/one/many-item boundaries to catch off-by-one errors.

items.title: Java 16: records and finalized pattern matching for instanceof
items.text: Modern Java features can make data modeling and branching clearer. Check the release baseline for each feature and keep preview-only syntax out of the stable core examples.

items.title: Java 17: sealed classes
items.text: A class defines state and behavior; an object is an instance. Encapsulation protects invariants by keeping mutable state private and validating updates through a small public API.
